Replay

Replay room service

6 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Local CavecrawlConfigurationDurable checkpointsVerification

Run this standalone Godot/Odin service to enroll room members, coordinate which process may accept gameplay results, and connect peers through RTC signaling. Its admission hub persists credentials; its authority coordinator grants and checks time-bounded hosting leases. It supports one game content ID and up to 32 resident rooms (16 by default). Native clients can use ENet gameplay; browser clients use RTC. The service stores and transfers durable checkpoints for the compiled Cavecrawl, Speedball, Scrapyard, Quickdraw, Claimball, Slopball, and Slopball3D models. It does not run gameplay; checkpoint download does not grant authority or automatically resume a game.

The bundled SQLite service currently runs on macOS/Linux. Both frameworks and all original games remain separate. This is an experimental deployment example, not a hosted service or a completed Internet operational profile.

Local Cavecrawl#

From the repository root, create a private data directory and start the service:

Shell
mkdir -m 700 -p .replay-room-data
REPLAY_ROOM_CONTENT=0x4341564552504c39 \
REPLAY_ROOM_DB="$PWD/.replay-room-data/rooms.sqlite3" \
REPLAY_ROOM_CREATE_DB=1 REPLAY_ROOM_LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT=1 \
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_room_service/run.sh

Creation is explicit. On subsequent runs omit REPLAY_ROOM_CREATE_DB=1, so losing the database does not silently erase previous authority decisions.

In another terminal:

Shell
REPLAY_CAVE_ROOM_SERVICE=ws://127.0.0.1:49740 \
REPLAY_CAVE_ROOM_LOCAL=1 \
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_cavecrawl/play.sh

Choose Create party, then share Copy party invite. Another player pastes it and chooses Join party. Rejoin recent party loads that game's stored credential. See the game flow for profile separation, gameplay addresses, browser use and recovery boundaries.

Configuration#

Environment variable Meaning
REPLAY_ROOM_CONTENT Required nonzero decimal or 0x hexadecimal game content ID
REPLAY_ROOM_CHECKPOINT_MODEL Optional required model: cavecrawl, cavecrawl-owned, speedball, scrapyard, quickdraw, claimball, slopball, slopball3d; disabled turns checkpoint endpoints off. By default, a matching compiled content ID enables its model; other content IDs remain admission-only
REPLAY_ROOM_DB Required private SQLite file path; protect its directory/backups
REPLAY_ROOM_CREATE_DB=1 Explicit first-time database creation
REPLAY_ROOM_BIND Listener address, default 127.0.0.1
REPLAY_ROOM_PORT Listener port, default 49740
REPLAY_ROOM_CAPACITY Resident/persisted room limit, 1–32, default 16
REPLAY_ROOM_CERT, REPLAY_ROOM_KEY TLS certificate/chain and private-key file paths
REPLAY_ROOM_LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT=1 Permit plain WS only on literal 127.0.0.1 or ::1
REPLAY_ROOM_MODE New-room policy: cooperative (default) or dedicated
REPLAY_ROOM_TURN_SECRET_FILE Optional server-only Coturn shared-secret file
REPLAY_ROOM_TURN_URLS Comma-separated TURN endpoints for credential issuance
REPLAY_ROOM_TURN_TTL Credential lifetime, 5–3600 seconds, default 600
REPLAY_ROOM_TURN_RELAY_ONLY=1 Require relay-only ICE in issued settings

The optional relay provider authenticates enabled members through a connection-bound challenge and issues expiring credentials. Clients never receive the signing secret. Coturn uses the same server-only secret with use-auth-secret; the client helper refreshes credentials in the background.

Without explicit loopback development mode, certificate/key material is required. The client must verify the certificate and hostname. Public browser origins need appropriate HTTPS/WSS deployment and reachable ICE/TURN infrastructure; those deployment gates remain open. The loopback fixture is not evidence of Internet reachability.

Dedicated mode refuses public creation of infrastructure credentials. Preload dedicated rooms using trusted admission administration. Existing records retain their policies; changing the new-room mode does not rewrite them. The service rejects wrong-content/corrupt or excessive startup inventories rather than dropping records to fit capacity.

Durable checkpoints#

The deployment's content ID selects validation code; client requests cannot select a model or schema. An explicit model/content mismatch fails before opening the database. Match this value to the game build’s CONTENT constant; changing it selects a different compatibility contract. Current compiled models are:

Model Content ID
Cavecrawl 0x4341564552504c39
Cavecrawl with owner observations 0x434156454f574e33
Speedball 0x5253504545444234
Scrapyard 0x525343524150304b
Quickdraw 0x52515549434b4432
Claimball 0x52434c41494d4233
Slopball 0x52534c4f50423234
Slopball3D 0x52534c4f50334434

Each admitted room receives one bounded checkpoint endpoint. Unknown-room traffic does not create endpoints, load storage or restart coordinators. Metadata and checkpoint bytes commit atomically with publication and a compare-and-swap (CAS) against the full coordinator Record. A final authorization guard rejects a lease that expires during validation or storage work. A normal player cannot read authority-only checkpoints; reads require trusted hosting permission, and dedicated rooms additionally require infrastructure.

Use the checkpoint client API on the same connection as the registered authority RPC. Upload/download/status packets are signed, and the service multiplexes them with admission, authority, signaling and relay traffic. Each endpoint holds at most one 1 MiB transfer with a 30-second lifetime and bounded packet budgets. Room capacity bounds the total endpoint count. An exact committed retry returns its publication without renewing authority.

This stores the game model's complete checkpoint, including embedded definitions and its declared external asset bytes. Scrapyard's current and executable pending spray dependencies use a complete atomic package, validated by the service and installed before restoration. Personal profiles remain separate. Room/Party handles manual/automatic publication; game integrations must supply UI and asset preparation. Recovery after all members leave requires the complete Room/Party restore flow. The service supports an explicit published restore grant: expired-owner registration remains lease/quarantine fenced, then a separate CAS authorizes an exact saved publication under a newer epoch. Native model fixtures exercise this. Room/Party drives it through Cavecrawl's native/browser rejoin menu, with callback-gated asset preparation. Scrapyard also passes native/browser restoration after deleting its local spray copy. Broader asset profiles and game acceptance remain open. Slopball has native WSS and browser RTC acceptance for restoring its published owner-streamed world and first actual solver momentum after all game processes and the service stop; see its restore flow. Slopball3D also has native/browser acceptance for quaternion and angular-momentum recovery, including restoration by another trusted saved player before the creator returns; see the 3D flow.

All binary admission and control packets share the socket. An initial RTC text message selects a current opaque room code; the existing challenge/MAC still authenticates that connection against that room's registered members. Later signals stay bound to the selected room. Room/epoch changes and poisoned coordinators close their signaling connections. Other rooms retain their own mappings and state.

This service owns its whole room set. Concurrent copies using the same database fence each other's CAS writes; this is not a highly available coordinator cluster. Anonymous co-op creation is bounded by the hub's room and request limits. Account authorization, per-user quotas, room retirement, public abuse controls and operational monitoring remain additional deployment work.

Verification#

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_cavecrawl/online_run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_cavecrawl/online_web_run.sh
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_room_checkpoint/run.sh
CHECKPOINT_RESTORE=1 nix develop --command bash tests/replay_room_checkpoint/run.sh

These drive actual menus, durable enrollment, automatic successor selection, handoff, loot conservation and fresh-process rejoin. Browser acceptance includes two simultaneous isolated rooms. Native uses verified fixture TLS; browser uses explicit loopback WS and real RTC. See recorded evidence.

The original checkpoint gate used the standalone service and three game models over verified TLS. The fixture publishes and downloads a tick-1 checkpoint, kills the service, reopens the same database, and verifies the identical archive from a fresh trusted incarnation 2 with zero authority lease. It also rejects mismatched deployment models before database creation. This is native seeded-state persistence evidence. Cavecrawl's native/browser Room tests additionally publish during active play and after migration. Its party_restore_run.sh and party_restore_web_run.sh gates resume actual saved cave play after every original process has exited, then admit a new guest and publish the continued game.
